rca of the issue: Original iteration_18 fix used a fixed ±25% midprice threshold, which was insensitive to the real 5.8%-off cluster (iteration_19 finding). Iteration_20 fix replaces fixed threshold with robust Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) filter: compute median of midprices, compute MAD, reject any row whose HIGH or LOW deviates from median by more than max(6*MAD, 0.1% of median). This adapts to each pair's own volatility — for the EUR/USD (OTC) batch (median 1.066), MAD is small so 6*MAD is tight and 5.8%-off rows fall well outside. For a volatile pair (e.g. crypto with 3%+ MAD), the band expands to preserve legitimate movement. Reproduction: navigate to /demo-trade EUR/USD (OTC) 1m; confirm no candle bodies float at 1.128 — chart now caps at ~1.104. Backend root-cause (bad persisted rows) still present; frontend fix is defensive but sufficient for user-facing correctness.
